run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-101 had issues on November 23, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: What the evidence shows for the app-101 payment-api: the only log stream Loki holds anywhere in this cluster is job=payment-api in namespace app-101 (service=payment-api, pod=payment-api-101-8486559b69-g48zg, file /var/log/payment-api.log). In that stream the reported 13:45 UTC period is marked by a burst of 8 ERROR lines reading exactly 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted', the first at 2026-11-23T13:46:00Z (wait_time_ms 1227, queue_length 10) and the last at 14:44:00Z (wait_time_ms 3836, queue_length 5); waits reached 4840 ms and queue lengths 5–15. In the 24h ending 18:40 UTC the stream returned only these 8 ERROR lines and 28 INFO 'Payment processed successfully' lines, and over 10:00–13:46 UTC it returned 5 lines, all INFO successes with no ERROR, so the failures began at 13:46 and were not preceded by errors in the observed log. Payments did not stop completely: INFO successes are present at 13:42, 13:59 and 14:49. No cause deeper than the pool exhaustion is established: the payment-api Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod from the incident no longer exists (namespace app-101 itself was created 2026-11-23T18:45:02Z, and the pod carrying that name was scheduled/started 18:45:25Z and had its containers stopped 18:45:37Z), so DB host, pool size and env settings cannot be read; Loki holds no database logs; and Prometheus and Jaeger both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt, so no metric or trace signal for this or the similarly named otel-demo 'payment' service could be assessed. Cluster-level shortfalls were checked and not found: no NetworkPolicy and no ResourceQuota exists. Hypotheses (unverified): a slow/unavailable database backend, or an undersized/leaking connection pool in payment-api, each of which would produce this exact message.

claims.text: Loki holds exactly one log stream for 2026-11-23: job=payment-api, namespace=app-101, service=payment-api. A grouping query over 06:00–18:40 UTC by namespace and job returned that single series, and the returned lines carry filename=/var/log/payment-api.log and pod=payment-api-101-8486559b69-g48zg.

The first observed failure is an ERROR line at 2026-11-23T13:46:00Z with message 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted', wait_time_ms 1227 and queue_length 10 from service payment-api, pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-g48zg.

All 8 ERROR lines in 13:40–16:00 UTC carry the same message 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' and occur at 13:46 (wait 1227 ms, queue 10), 13:54 (2104 ms, 11), 14:03 (1495 ms, 8), 14:15 (2965 ms, 9), 14:19 (4005 ms, 10), 14:21 (4840 ms, 8), 14:31 (2358 ms, 15) and 14:44 (3836 ms, 5).

In the 24 hours ending 2026-11-23T18:40:00Z the payment-api stream returned only two distinct messages: 8 ERROR 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' and 28 INFO 'Payment processed successfully'.

Before the incident the stream showed no errors: the complete result for 10:00–13:46 UTC is 5 lines, all INFO 'Payment processed successfully' (11:19, 11:40, 11:44, 12:57, 13:42), with 0 lines omitted by the 200-line limit.

The failure was intermittent, not a total outage: INFO 'Payment processed successfully' lines are present inside the error period at 13:59:00Z (PAY-1800) and after it at 14:49:00Z (PAY-8206), alongside a success at 13:42:00Z (PAY-5032) just before it.
The namespace holding the payment-api did not exist at incident time: namespace app-101 was created 2026-11-23T18:45:02Z, while the log payload's own timestamps run 13:42–14:49 UTC.

The pod named in the log payload, payment-api-101-8486559b69-g48zg, was scheduled, created and started at 18:45:25Z by ReplicaSet payment-api-101-8486559b69 after Deployment payment-api-101 scaled that ReplicaSet 0→1, and both of its containers (payment-api, promtail) were stopped 'Killing' at 18:45:37Z; the current pod list for app-101 contains only loki-66445c6d6f-lkdls and the app-101 Deployment list contains only loki.

The app-101 namespace objects describe a purpose-built log replay stack: ConfigMap promtail-config declares job_name payment-api with labels job=payment-api and namespace app-101 scraping /var/log/*.log, and ConfigMap loki-config sets a 2-year max_query_lookback/reject_old_samples_max_age so old-timestamped lines are retained.

Cluster-level plumbing was checked and is not the explanation: no NetworkPolicy and no ResourceQuota exists anywhere in the cluster, so connection failures cannot be attributed to a policy or quota object.

Against a pod-crash/resource-failure explanation: the app's own diagnostic text names database connection acquisition with an exhausted pool, and among the 26 events returned across all namespaces for the visible event window (18:27:05–18:46:26 UTC) there is no OOMKilled, Evicted, BackOff, Failed or Unhealthy reason for any app-101 pod — the app-101 reasons are only ScalingReplicaSet, SuccessfulCreate, Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started and Killing.

The similarly named but different entity in otel-demo was checked: pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm (Deployment payment, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment) is Running and ready with restartCount 0, started 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z — after the incident window — and it is not the app-101 payment-api asked about.

The database backend that payment-api connects to was slow or unavailable around 13:46–14:44 UTC, which would leave checkout threads waiting 1.2–4.8 s for a connection, queue up to 15 waiters and exhaust the pool. Unverified: no database logs or database metrics exist in any available source and the DB host is not named in any visible object or line.

Alternatively payment-api's own connection pool was undersized or leaking, so that normal demand exhausted it and every acquisition waited until failure. Unverified: the Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod spec that would carry pool size, DB host and connection env is no longer present, so this cannot be confirmed or excluded.

Retrieve the payment-api-101 Deployment/pod template (DB host env, connection-pool size and timeout settings) and the database server's own logs and latency, then compare pool saturation and DB response time over 13:46–14:44 UTC before deciding between the backend-slowness and pool-configuration hypotheses.

gaps: Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable throughout this run: execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values, traces_list_services and traces_search all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (5 attempts, latest 2026-11-23T18:48:52Z), so no metric or trace signal exists here for the app-101 payment-api or for the otel-demo payment service; their error and latency behaviour during 13:45 UTC is unassessed, not healthy.

The payment-api-101 Deployment, ReplicaSet payment-api-101-8486559b69 and pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-g48zg are gone (app-101 currently lists only Deployment loki and pod loki-66445c6d6f-lkdls; fetch_pod_logs for that pod returned POD_NOT_FOUND), so container status, last termination reason, exit code, previous-container logs and the pod template with DB/pool settings are unknown.

No database-side evidence: the only Loki stream in the cluster is job=payment-api/app-101, so whatever service payment-api's database is has no logs or metrics here and cannot be identified or checked.

Kubernetes events covering 13:45 UTC are not available: the returned events only span 18:27:05–18:46:26 UTC, so event absence at incident time is unknown rather than evidence. A Loki query for level=ERROR over 06:00–13:45 UTC returned no lines (no_data, not usable as a fact); the error-free baseline rests on the complete 10:00–13:46 UTC line set.

The incident-time timeline could not be corroborated at pod level: namespace app-101 was created 2026-11-23T18:45:02Z and the log payload's pod name matches a pod created 18:45:25Z and killed at 18:45:37Z, so the 13:42–14:49 UTC timestamps come from the application's own JSON timestamp field only and the namespace/pod objects do not describe the incident-time runtime.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this run, so no record of deployments, config edits or restarts around 13:45 UTC could be consulted.

The payment-api log lines are sparse (28 INFO lines per 24h; 8 ERROR lines), so no request rate, success ratio or duration trend can be computed for the incident window; only the individual observed lines are evidence.
next_steps: Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access and query the app-101 payment-api's error/latency series and the otel-demo payment service for 13:40–15:00 UTC to see whether a backend dependency also degraded.

Obtain the payment-api-101 Deployment manifest or pod template (DB host, max pool size, acquire timeout) from cluster backup or change history, and compare it with the 4840 ms acquires and queue lengths of 5–15 observed.
Collect the database server's logs and connection/latency metrics for 2026-11-23T13:40:00Z–15:00:00Z to test whether connections were slow or refused.

Confirm with the application owner whether the 13:42–14:49 UTC log file is a replayed capture placed in the app-101 pod at 18:45Z, and if so locate the original pod's kubelet status and previous-container logs from that time.

view.cannot_prove: A line that is not returned is unknown, not proof that nothing was logged: only limit lines are shown (the newest), and retention, ingest delay, the label selector and line filters can leave gaps. The timestamp is when the line was ingested or parsed, not necessarily when the event happened. A metric query counts only lines inside the query window.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
